How this book matches your board exam. Research check: this book follows NCERT Class 12 Business Studies Part 1, Chapter 1 (Nature and Significance of Management), for the CBSE 2026–27 session. Chapter 1 is in Part A, Principles and Functions of Management (50 marks); Units 1–3 together carry 16 marks. The theory paper is 80 marks, 3 hours, with 20 marks for project work. Recent sample papers have 34 questions: 20 × 1 mark, 4 × 3 marks, 6 × 4 marks and 4 × 6 marks. Case-based questions are common.

Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set. The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme. Businesses in examples are invented.

Unit 1 of 10: Concept of Management: Effectiveness and Efficiency

Key ideas

  • Management is the process of getting things done with the aim of achieving goals effectively and efficiently.
  • Process: a series of primary functions — planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling.
  • Effectiveness: completing the work on time — achieving the end result (doing the right task).
  • Efficiency: doing the task correctly at minimum cost — the ratio of output to inputs (doing the task right).
  • Good management needs both: a firm that meets its target but wastes resources is effective but not efficient; a firm that saves cost but misses its target is efficient but not effective.

Worked examples

Example 1: Kirana Foods produced its target of 10,000 packets on time but spent 20% more on raw materials than planned. Answer: effective (target met on time) but not efficient (cost was too high).

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) Efficiency in management means: (a) completing work on time (b) doing work correctly at minimum cost (c) setting goals (d) hiring staff. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) Define effectiveness. Answer: completing the right task and achieving the goal on time.
  3. (3 marks) Distinguish between effectiveness and efficiency. Answer: effectiveness concerns the end result/on-time completion (1); efficiency concerns minimum use of resources/cost (1); management needs a balance of both (1).
  4. (2 marks) A factory achieved its target by using extra overtime at high cost. Identify which aspect was achieved and which was missed. Answer: effectiveness achieved (1); efficiency missed (1).
  5. (3 marks) Explain the meaning of management with its three key elements. Answer: a process — a series of functions (1); effectiveness — achieving goals on time (1); efficiency — minimum cost (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Swapping effectiveness and efficiency. 2. Defining management as "managing people" only. 3. Missing "process". 4. Saying only one is needed. 5. No example.

Quick recall

  1. Management? 2. Effectiveness? 3. Efficiency? 4. Can a firm be effective but not efficient? 5. Number of primary functions?

Answers: 1) Getting things done effectively and efficiently. 2) Achieving goals on time. 3) Minimum cost. 4) Yes. 5) Five.
